content: Sometimes, lesions associated with porokeratosis may exhibit significant overgrowth, and in some cases, horn-like structures can develop. Although rare, skin malignancies have been reported in all types of porokeratosis. Squamous cell carcinoma has been documented to arise in the Mibelli type of porokeratosis, particularly in areas involving the anal mucosa. This was the first reported case highlighting mucosal malignancy in any form of porokeratosis. Porokeratosis of Mibelli is also referred to as Steinberg's lesion. It was first characterized in 1970. From a pathological perspective, porokeratosis is defined by a distinct histomorphologic feature known as the cornoid lamella.
